newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says to cut salaries of top personnel.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says to cut salaries of top personnel.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it would cut the salaries of its president and its chairman by 30 percent for five months.

Nomura president Junichi Ujiie announced the salary cuts at a news conference after the Finance Ministry disclosed penalties against the brokerage for its role in a scandal involving illegal payoffs to a corporate racketeer.
Ujiie said that the salaries of executive directors would be cut by 20 percent, while those of managing directors would be reduced by 15 percent.
He also said that the ministry's penalties will have a considerable impact on the company's earnings for the current business year.

Ujiie said that one direct effect of the penalties will be a decline in services it can offer to institutional investors, as the company's equities section that trades on its own account will not be able to take on orders for large-lot and basket trades.
He also said the company would strive to post profits in the current business year, but added that he could not say for certain whether results for the year would be in the black.

Asked about the possible filing of a lawsuit by Nomura against its former president Hideo Sakamaki and other executives who have been indicted by prosecutors, Ujiie said: "We cannot say that we are not thinking about it."
